title: Help Getting Food
intro: If money is tight, you do not have to go hungry. Some help is free for anyone. Some depends on your income. Start with the step that fits you.

emergency.title: Need food today?
emergency.text: Dial 211 any time to find food near you, or text your ZIP code to 898-211.

who.title: Who may qualify
who.text: Pantries and food maps are open to anyone. SNAP and WIC have income limits. Meals on Wheels is for older adults who need help getting meals.
who.fine: Not sure if you qualify? Apply anyway. The program will tell you.

programs.name: Westbrook Community Food & Resource Center
programs.summary: The city’s volunteer food pantry at the Westbrook Community Center. Open every Tuesday from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m.
programs.know: First time? Bring proof you live in Westbrook, like a utility bill or rent bill. Hours can change, so call if you are not sure.

programs.name: Vineyard Church Food Pantry
programs.summary: A church pantry at 715 Bridgton Road. Food is handed out on Fridays starting at 5:45 p.m. It serves Westbrook and Portland residents who live west of Riverside.
programs.know: Arrive by 5 p.m. and line up in your car. Hours can change, so call the church office if you are not sure.
programs.sourceLabel: Wayside Food Programs; times confirmed by a pantry coordinator, Oct 16, 2026

programs.name: The Locker Project at Walker Memorial Library
programs.summary: Free fresh food for anyone to take home, on the first Thursday of each month in the library’s Youth Program Room. Next visits: Nov. 5 and Dec. 3.
programs.know: Bring a bag or box if you can. Dates can change, so check the City calendar or call the Locker Project.

programs.name: Good Shepherd Food Bank: Food Map
programs.summary: A map of pantries, meal sites and other food help across Maine. It includes a mobile pantry called the Food Mobile.
programs.know: Open the official page and choose the Food Map. Check hours with each place before you go.

programs.name: 211 Maine
programs.summary: A free help line that can point you to food and other help near you.
programs.know: You can also text your ZIP code to 898-211.

programs.name: SNAP (Food Supplement)
programs.summary: Money on a card (EBT) each month to buy groceries. The limit depends on how many people are in your home.
programs.know: Apply online, by phone or at a state office. The state has 30 days to decide, and you will have an interview. Over the limit? Some households still qualify, so you can apply anyway. Phone lines are open Monday to Friday, 7 to 4.

programs.name: WIC
programs.summary: Food, nutrition help and breastfeeding support for people who are pregnant or breastfeeding, and for children up to age 5.
programs.know: If you get MaineCare, SNAP or TANF, you already meet the income rule. Use the form on the official page, and WIC staff will call you to set up a visit.

programs.name: Meals on Wheels
programs.summary: Meals brought to your home by the Southern Maine Agency on Aging. It is for people age 60 and older who are mostly homebound and cannot easily make meals.
programs.know: A $3.50 gift per meal is suggested. No one is turned away if they cannot pay. Fill out the online form or call. The page says it serves York and Cumberland counties.

programs.name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP)
programs.summary: Free USDA foods each month to add to a senior’s groceries.
programs.know: Wayside Food Programs handles sign-ups for Cumberland County, including Westbrook. Call or use the form on their site. Income limits change each year, so ask when you call.

programs.name: Community Cafes
programs.chip: Call to ask who can come
programs.summary: Lunches with other people, run by the Southern Maine Agency on Aging in York and Cumberland counties.
programs.know: Ask which cafes are close to Westbrook, and what days they meet.

programs.name: Westbrook General Assistance
programs.summary: City help for basic needs when other programs are not enough. Appointment only, no walk-ins.
programs.know: Based on income for 30 days at a time. You must apply to other programs first.
